svg.title: The coordinate parametrization is an isomorphism for simple g. The equation-of-motion vector is the image of (1, −1/4, 1), which (TR52) annihilates. More generally, if the vector belongs to the equation ideal, its coordinates satisfy 2(w0 −w2) = 0 and 2w1 + 1 2w2 = 0; these force ρ = 0. The field-space functional L is ρ after the degree-five coordinate isomorphism. This proves both its equation-of-motion annihilation and the readings 0, −4 on the two columns of (TR45). At finite level the same reading can be computed before quotienting. For a real regular local vector V = (Va), the coefficient functional M on its degree-five cards satisfies
